anomalies.observed: U10 and U11 are isolated CAN transceivers (CA-IS3050G). Their logic-side ground pins GND1 (pin 4) and bus-side ground pins GND2 (pin 5) are both connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: GND1 should connect to logic ground, and GND2 should connect to an isolated bus ground (separate net) to maintain galvanic isolation.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier is shorted, so the CAN buses are no longer isolated; ground loops and noise can couple between the logic and bus sides, defeating the purpose of the isolated transceivers.

anomalies.observed: D30 is a dual LED. Its second LED has anode A2 (pin 4) on ESTOP_OUT and cathode K2 (pin 2) connected through R60 to the same ESTOP_OUT net (R60.2 is on ESTOP_OUT, R60.1 is on Net-(D30-K2) with D30.2).
anomalies.expected: The cathode K2 should connect through R60 to ground (or a return path) so the LED can light when ESTOP_OUT is high.
anomalies.impact: The second LED in D30 will never illuminate because both its anode and cathode are tied to the same net through a resistor; e-stop indication is lost.

anomalies.observed: U21 is an FT231XS USB-UART. Its internal 3.3V LDO output pin 3V3OUT (pin 13) is connected to the +3V3 net, which is also connected to its VCC (pin 15) and VCCIO (pin 3).
anomalies.expected: When the FT231XS is powered from 3.3V on VCC, the 3V3OUT pin should be left unconnected (or not tied to the same 3.3V rail) to avoid conflict with the external 3.3V regulator.
anomalies.impact: The internal LDO output fights the external 3.3V regulator, potentially causing excessive current, instability, or damage to U21 or U20.

parsed.summary: The design files contain multiple anomalies. The most critical is that the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have their logic-side and bus-side grounds tied together, defeating galvanic isolation. Additionally, the second LED in D30 is shorted and will never light, and the FT231XS U21 has its internal 3.3V LDO output tied to the external 3.3V rail, creating an output conflict.
